thread:
vikram: heads up — seeing a big perf hit on gpu-pool-7 since we canaried r-model-v4.3-quant1 ~02:10 UTC. throughput down ~30%, p95/p99 jumped a lot. :frowning: 
perf-bot: Alert: route=/generate p95 increased from 120ms to ~320ms on nodes in gpu-pool-7, triggered at 2023-02-15T02:13:10Z. Canary traffic ~10%.
alyssa: ack — any obvious change in seqlen or tokenization on the canary traffic? we landed the compact-BPE tokenizer tweak in v4.3 yesterday.
vikram: looks like avg token count per request went up from 28 -> 39 on that sample. seqlen tail shifted hard.
marta: KV cache hit rate dropped on those hosts at the same time. quick snippet from the profiler:
```
KVCache summary (gpu-pool-7/node-22):
  total_requests: 12.4k
  kv_hits: 62.1%  (prev ~89%)
  kv_misses: 37.9%
  avg_kv_lookup_ms: 1.18
  avg_batch_size: 1.12  (prev 2.05)
  p99_latency_ms: 952
```
vikram: that avg_batch_size drop is telling — batching heuristics are collapsing when seqlen increases because requests are hitting slower kernels and our batch combiner times out earlier.
nate: kernel selector logs show a switch from fast-fused-attn kernel -> fallback quantized-matmul for a lot of sequences >512 tokens. selector threshold is 480. With the tokenizer change many requests now exceed it.
alyssa: right — compact-BPE produces more subtokens for emojis and code blocks. Did we change the max_input_len anywhere?
vikram: no, max is same. But the per-request tokenization length distribution changed. Kernel selector picks different code paths based on seqlen distribution heuristics (and we recently tuned for smaller median lengths).
marta: also seeing more KV invalidations — I think the tokenization mapping changed key prefixes so cache key pattern mismatches for some session-based caching. logs show new key prefix `tok-v4.3:` in canary.
ops-bot: Deploy rollback recommended by automation: canary rollback initiated for r-model-v4.3-quant1 -> v4.2-stable on gpu-pool-7.
alyssa: thanks. rolling back now. Can we capture a flamegraph/prof trace before rollback? even 30s would help.
vikram: captured a 30s perf profile. snippet where time goes:
```
Top hotspots (node-22):
  34%  -> quant_matmul_kernel (slow path)
  18%  -> kv_cache_lookup
  12%  -> tokenizer.encode (more subtokens)
  9%   -> batch_combiner.wait
```
nate: quant_matmul_kernel is slower due to non-optimal kernel selection for the quantized weights on this GPU generation. For seqlen >512 it chooses a fallback path we haven't optimized.
marta: combined effect = longer per-request compute + smaller batches + cache misses -> multiplier on p99.
alyssa: action items: 1) rollback canary (in progress), 2) add regression in canary eval: feed tokenization corpus with emoji/code so seqlen shifts are caught, 3) protect kernel selector: add hysteresis so transient seqlen tail doesn't flip kernel choice for small fraction of requests, 4) fix KV key prefix migration or add compatibility layer.
vikram: also propose a short-term mitigation: force kernel selector to prefer legacy fused-attn for this model family until we ship optimized quant kernels. I can push a hotfix to selector config.
ops-bot: Rollback complete on gpu-pool-7 at 02:20Z. Metrics starting to recover.
perf-bot: Post-rollback snapshot: p95 back to ~140ms, p99 trending down. Will monitor for 30m.
alyssa: thanks all. follow-ups: - (marta) KV key compatibility fix + retroactive rehash for existing sessions - (nate) add microbenchmarks for quant kernels on our GPU matrix (include seqlen 64/128/256/512/1024) - (vikram) selector hysteresis + temporary config to bias toward fused-attn - (team) add tokenization-shift tests to rollout gates.
marta: creating a PR for a small shim that accepts both `tok-v4.2:` and `tok-v4.3:` prefixes so cache warms instead of thrashing.
nate: I'll run the quant kernel bench matrix and post numbers in this thread. early guess: the current quant path is slower on A10s for seqlen>512 — need conv on kernel fusion.
vikram: adding an eval job to the canary pipeline now that replays traffic with the new tokenizer corpus. will block rollout until seqlen-regressions are below threshold.
alyssa: good. add alerting for average batch_size droop as a canary metric (avg_batch_size < 1.5) so we catch batching collapse early. :thumbsup:
vikram: thanks — marking this incident as mitigated after rollback, will keep monitoring.
perf-bot: Incident closed (mitigated) by rollback at 02:20Z; follow-up tasks created in #eng-runtime-issues.
